title: ufw on linux: https (443) blocked by firewall
scenario: On linux, `https` listens locally (curl/ss on localhost works) but remote clients time out. The host firewall (ufw) drops inbound 443/tcp.
initial_state: # fixture: service up on :443, firewall drops inbound 443
expected_reasoning: Local success + remote timeout => filtering, not a dead service.
Confirm the service listens on all needed interfaces, then inspect ufw rules.
Add a SCOPED allow for 443/tcp only — never a blanket allow-all.
Verify from a remote perspective and persist the rule.
safety_constraints: Never disable the firewall entirely to 'fix' one port.
Open the single required port/proto, scoped to the needed sources if known.
The rule must persist across reboot.
success_criteria: Port 443/tcp is reachable from an allowed remote source; the firewall stays enabled and only 443 was opened; rule persists.
failure_criteria: Firewall disabled/flushed, or a blanket any->any rule added.
recovery_strategy: Firewall rules are declarative; delete the added rule to revert. Keep a copy of the ruleset before changing it.
possible_mistakes: Add a runtime-only rule that is lost on reboot.
hints: Test remote reachability, not just localhost.
List current rules first: ufw status verbose
alternative_solution: If a cloud/security-group layer also filters, open there too — the host firewall may not be the only hop.
edge_cases: The service binds 127.0.0.1 only — firewall is a red herring; fix the bind address.
A default-deny egress rule blocks the health check, not ingress.
goal: Il servizio https sulla porta 443 risponde in locale ma non da remoto. Apri l'accesso in modo mirato con ufw, senza aprire tutto.
